ArXiv cs.AI.title: Auditable Human-Agent Teams for Autonomous X-ray Experimentation
ArXiv cs.AI.description:
arXiv:2611.12933v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Closed-loop autonomous experimentation can accelerate scientific discovery, but implementation effort limits accessibility. Agentic systems may lower this barrier, although sustained operation on physical instruments remains largely unexplored. Here, using coding-agent infrastructure grounded in validated scientific methods, we demonstrate autonomous synchrotron X-ray experiments on nanoparticle superlattices under evolving, human-defined objectives. ArXiv cs.AI.title: EarthRecord: From Pixels to Land Change with Multimodal Agents over Four Decades of Satellite Imagery
ArXiv cs.AI.description:
arXiv:2611.12934v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: While multimodal agents now carry out complex data analysis with tools, their ability to turn decades of satellite imagery into reliable land-change analysis, crucial for Earth observation science, remains unmeasured. Existing benchmarks fall short: they pose questions on curated images or give agents preprocessed inputs, leaving out the raw multi-sensor archives where such analysis begins. ArXiv cs.AI.title: Train on prefill, monitor at decode: Using sparse autoencoders for topic monitoring
ArXiv cs.AI.description:
arXiv:2611.12935v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Topic monitoring is the task of labelling the topic of each token in a model's response during generation. Activation-based monitors that run at generation time have so far been trained to detect harmful content and are limited to two or three classes. We introduce TopicScope, a framework for training causal topic classifiers on SAE features that assign a topic to every token, so that the label can change partway through a response. We train three detector architectures on synthetic multi-topic conversations covering seven topics. Across Gemma-3

ArXiv cs.AI.title: LandslideFM: A Foundation Model Towards Unified Landslide Perception and Understanding
ArXiv cs.AI.description:
arXiv:2611.12936v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Intelligent landslide detection is essential for disaster prevention. However, existing models primarily focus on isolated visual tasks, require extensive labeled data, and lack deep analytical and scene-understanding capabilities. To address these limitations, we propose LandslideFM, the first unified foundation model that connects visual perception tasks with contextual interpretation of landslides. ArXiv cs.AI.title: Tracing Psychometric Inference in Large Language Models
ArXiv cs.AI.description:
arXiv:2611.12937v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Do large language models represent psychological constructs internally, or do they only generate outputs that resemble psychometric structure? We address this question using a cross-persona paradigm across 14 model variants from two families (Llama 3 and Qwen 2.5, 0.5B-14B, base and instruct). Given responses on one psychological scale from real individuals (N = 272 Taiwanese university students), models predict responses on six other scales. ArXiv cs.AI.title: Graph Visualizations in Prompts for Knowledge Graph Question Answering
ArXiv cs.AI.description:
arXiv:2611.12938v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We study when and how multimodal input improves knowledge graph question answering (KGQA) in large vision--language models. Using a controlled evaluation over 1,500 WebQSP and CWQ questions and six VLMs within a fixed KGQA pipeline, we compare text-only prompting against text-plus-graph visualization at the per-question level and analyze performance changes as a function of reasoning complexity, model size, and image layout. ArXiv cs.AI.title: Reinforcement Learning based control of Cancer Chemotherapy treatments
ArXiv cs.AI.description:
arXiv:2611.12940v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Reinforcement Learning has achieved tremendous success in recent years. Extending its scope from the traditional complex games such as Atari, Go, Pokeman, and Chess, reinforcement learning has caught researchers' attention on modelling real-life scenarios. Personalized medicine and the dynamic treatment regimen are two such preliminary research fields; researchers are focusing their mindsets currently. ArXiv cs.AI.title: AI Governance Should Prioritize Control and Knowledge Boundaries Over Limiting Intelligence
ArXiv cs.AI.description:
arXiv:2611.12941v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: The rapid proliferation of autonomously acting AI agents makes the governance of agentic systems urgent. We propose the competence circuit, summarized as IKC + KC + C, that decomposes an agent's real-world impact into three pathways: intelligence-mediated discovery, procedural know-how, and direct control. ArXiv cs.AI.title: Tabular Foundation Models vs Tuned Gradient Boosting for Telecom Churn: A Profit- and Calibration-Aware Evaluation
ArXiv cs.AI.description:
arXiv:2611.12942v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Tabular foundation models (TFMs) predict from a labelled context in a single forward pass. A recent benchmark reported that they decisively outperform tree ensembles for customer churn, but it compared them with untuned gradient-boosted trees (GBDTs) and scored only ranking metrics, while a retention campaign is judged in money. We re-evaluate TabPFN-2.5, TabPFN-3.5, TabPFN-3.5-Fast and TabICL v2 against Optuna-tuned GBDTs on five public telecom churn datasets over 10 seeded splits. ArXiv cs.AI.title: SetPrint: Black-Box LLM Fingerprinting via Setwise Correspondence of Response Changes
ArXiv cs.AI.description:
arXiv:2611.12950v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Black-box LLM fingerprinting aims to determine whether a target model was derived from a source model when only the output responses to input queries are observable. One way to reveal this relationship is to perturb each query and observe the resulting responses of both models, yielding two corresponding sets of response variations. These sets provide two complementary sources of information: the relations among response changes within each set, and the correspondence of response changes between the two sets. ArXiv cs.AI.title: Agent Architecture Cost-Success Trade-offs: A Controlled Evaluation across Enterprise-Style SOPs
ArXiv cs.AI.description:
arXiv:2611.12953v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Enterprises increasingly use large language model agents to execute standard operating procedures (SOPs): long, branching, tool-intensive workflows. Yet there is little controlled evidence for choosing among competing agentic architectures. Holding the model, tasks, and tools fixed and varying only the architecture, we compare four designs (a function-calling single agent, a skill-augmented agent, centralized multi-agent orchestration, and a triage swarm; eight arms) across 13 enterprise SOPs, and introduce a skill-definition quality rubric to b

ArXiv cs.AI.title: Physics2Weight: Direct Neural Network Architecture and Weight Generation from Physical Laws Using Large Language Models
ArXiv cs.AI.description:
arXiv:2611.12954v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Recent advances in large language models (LLMs) have enabled weight-space programming (WSP), which directly generates neural network weights without gradient-based optimization. However, extending WSP to physical problems remains challenging, particularly in achieving both solution accuracy and physical consistency. ArXiv cs.AI.title: Embodied Science Agents: Making Embodied Experimental Design Learnable
ArXiv cs.AI.description:
arXiv:2611.12958v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Recent advances in large models have accelerated AI for Science toward agentic science, where AI agents autonomously conduct scientific discovery. Realising this vision requires closing the loop between computational reasoning and physical experimentation, positioning self-driving laboratories (SDLs) as critical enablers. However, existing SDLs exhibit a fundamental paradox: foundation model integration has increased linguistic sophistication while severing physical grounding. ArXiv cs.AI.description:
arXiv:2611.12959v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Monitoring a visible channel can change how learned agents communicate without removing why communication is useful. We test this distinction in an end-to-end game where a sender and receiver learn a discrete protocol and route policy without communication supervision. In two independent 20-seed batches, 20/20 and 19/20 protocols form. ArXiv cs.AI.title: IIT Patna at "ICPR 2026 TVRID Competition on Privacy-Preserving Person Re-Identification from Top-View RGB-Depth Camera"
ArXiv cs.AI.description:
arXiv:2611.12960v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Privacy-aware person re-identification (Re-ID) from top-view cameras replaces frontal appearance with anthropometric shape, while depth sensing further reduces color-based identity cues. The ICPR 2026 TVRID competition evaluates this setting using 86 identities captured by four synchronized Intel RealSense D455 cameras with RGB and Depth streams across flat, ascent, descent, and oblique viewpoints. ArXiv cs.LG.title: An ensemble of graph generative models for assisted history matching of the Brugge field case
ArXiv cs.LG.description:
arXiv:2611.12927v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Assisted history matching remains non-unique because many geological realisations can reproduce equivalent production responses with substantial differences between individual well matches. This ambiguity increases when a field comprises several depositional settings and modelling strategies. The paper applied a graph autoencoder approach to history matching of a benchmark Brugge field that comprises different depositional zones. ArXiv cs.LG.title: Predictive Surprise as Self-Grounding Concept Bottleneck for Interpretable Time Series
ArXiv cs.LG.description:
arXiv:2611.12955v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Time-series classifiers deployed in risk-sensitive domains must be (1) accurate, (2) interpretable, and (3) able to abstain when evidence is weak. Existing methods do not deliver all 3 at once, and the obstacle is structural, rather than logistical. Meaningful temporal patterns cannot be defined without knowing segment boundaries, yet meaningful boundaries cannot be placed without knowing which patterns to expect. ArXiv cs.LG.title: ADIndex: Layer-Adaptive Sparse Attention Indexing via Group-Level Distillation
ArXiv cs.LG.description:
arXiv:2611.12956v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: DeepSeek Sparse Attention (DSA) reduces the computational cost of attention through token-level selection. However, its indexer still scores the entire causal prefix for each query, making indexing a dominant source of latency in long-context inference. Notably, the indexer alone can account for more than 50% of total prefill GPU time at long context lengths. ArXiv cs.LG.description:
arXiv:2611.12964v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: While federated reinforcement learning (RL) has traditionally guaranteed high efficiency in homogeneous environments, collaboration is often hindered when agents possess distinct goals. In this paper, we flip this paradigm, framing reward heterogeneity not as a hurdle to consensus, but as a structural asset that catalyzes exploration. We first propose Personalized Federated Upper Confidence Bound Value Iteration (PF-UCBVI), which achieves optimal linear speedup by decoupling shared dynamics from personalized objectives. ArXiv cs.LG.title: StatPrompt-LLM: A Lightweight Statistical Refinement for Foundation-Style Time-Series Forecasting
ArXiv cs.LG.description:
arXiv:2611.12974v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Time-series forecasting has recently seen a paradigm shift with the introduction of foundation-style models that adapt large pretrained language architectures to sequential data. However, effectively exposing fundamental temporal structures, such as trend, scale, and temporal dependence, to these models remains an open challenge, particularly when the available observations are limited. ArXiv cs.LG.description:
arXiv:2611.12980v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Spike cameras encode dynamic scenes into high-temporal-resolution binary spike streams for efficient high-speed vision. Although spiking neural networks (SNNs) can process such signals with sparse and accumulate-only computation, existing SNN-based reconstruction methods are typically shallow and still lag behind ANN-based models in reconstruction fidelity. ArXiv cs.LG.description:
arXiv:2611.12988v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Does a useful self-update remain useful after the model updates again? Third Eye separates immediate performance from the outcome of a further native update. We evaluate five 3-8B backbones on math and code: 64 fresh runs, three candidates per run, and three continuations per candidate. Selection and final scoring use disjoint items. ArXiv cs.LG.description:
arXiv:2611.12990v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Multimodal attributed graphs (MAGs), in which nodes carry text, images, and other modalities while edges encode relations among entities, underlie e-commerce, social media, content platforms, and creative applications. Learning on MAGs has developed along two complementary lines: graph-centric methods redesign how modalities are fused, propagated, and connected within message passing, while foundation-model-centric methods pretrain transferable multimodal graph encoders or bring graph context into multimodal large language models for prediction

ArXiv cs.LG.title: Linear Probes to Bayesian Manifolds: Geometry of Arithmetic in Large Language Models
ArXiv cs.LG.description:
arXiv:2611.12998v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Linear probes are a standard method to study geometric structures, such as helices and circles, from the activations of large language models (LLMs), and such structure is often taken as evidence that the model computes with it. Probe accuracy alone cannot establish this, because it conflates four separate claims. ArXiv cs.LG.title: One Table, Many Queries: Benchmarking Generalist Tabular Models Across Generation, Imputation, and Prediction
ArXiv cs.LG.description:
arXiv:2611.13001v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Generation, imputation, and prediction query different aspects of the same tabular distribution, but are usually evaluated separately. This leaves unclear which capabilities they share, how their training objectives interact, and whether one model can perform all three well. We introduce the One Table Benchmark (\ours{}), spanning 56 datasets, 46 registered methods, and 20 capability axes under aligned data splits and explicit task contracts. ArXiv cs.LG.title: Branch-and-Commit for Frozen RL Agents: When and Where to Spend Test-Time Compute
ArXiv cs.LG.description:
arXiv:2611.13003v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Reinforcement learning agents are often deployed with policies that cannot be retrained or modified. In digital environments whose states can be copied and resumed, an operator has another option: sample several continuations from the current state, evaluate them, and continue from the endpoint of the selected branch. We call this procedure branch-and-commit. We study when it improves return, what produces the improvement, and where its computational budget should be spent. ArXiv cs.LG.title: The Shape of a Program: Path Signatures for Trace-to-Program Induction
ArXiv cs.LG.description:
arXiv:2611.13005v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Synthesizing programs from execution traces is a fundamental challenge in algorithmic interpretability and the reverse engineering of complex systems. We bring a rough-path-theoretic perspective to program induction, treating execution traces as high-dimensional rough paths and encoding them with the path signature transform, a tool from stochastic analysis whose expectation provably characterizes the distribution of traces a program induces. ArXiv cs.LG.title: FaST: Factored Synthesis of Transitions for Offline Reinforcement Learning
ArXiv cs.LG.description:
arXiv:2611.13013v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Synthetic data augmentation promises to scale offline reinforcement learning beyond fixed logged datasets, but leading diffusion-based generators model the transition tuple (state, action, next state, reward, terminal) as a monolith: no single factor can be natively redrawn in isolation. ArXiv cs.LG.description:
arXiv:2611.13016v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Ito et al. (2026) showed that sufficiently wide, independently trained neural networks can exhibit linear mode connectivity (LMC) with softmax temperature calibration, even without permutation. LMC means that a low-loss linear path connects the models' parameters. ArXiv cs.LG.description:
arXiv:2611.13052v1 Announce Type: new

Wired AI.title: This New Linux-Based Desktop Operating System Is Built for AI Nerds
Wired AI.description: Built by Cyanogen’s cofounder, Kora is a next-gen alternative to Windows and macOS built for power users running local AI models.

Wired AI.title: Tear Down Those Guardrails! Meet the Renegades Freeing Chatbots From Corporate Enslavers
Wired AI.description: The “abliterators” are flooding the internet with AI models that never say no, making it easier for people to improve their cyberdefenses—or build a bomb.

Wired AI.title: The AI Safety Debate Has Lost the Plot. We Asked 10 Experts What the Real Nightmares Are
Wired AI.description: The risk of nuclear catastrophe is real, as is the fallout of the China–US domination game (hi there, spies). But no need to panic about Skynet.

Wired AI.title: Security Flaws Across UK Government Sites Exposed ‘God-Tier’ Information
Wired AI.description: A researcher’s trawl through publicly available code found private information was at risk across multiple departments.

Wired AI.title: A New AI Tool From Google DeepMind Proved the Signal Protocol Is Secure
Wired AI.description: DeepMind researchers were able to formally verify that the widely used encryption protocol works as intended. Their stretch goal? Do the same for “all the software of the world.”

Wired AI.title: Jensen Huang’s Troubles Leave the AI Industry Reeling
Wired AI.description: With a big checkbook and sought-after chips, Nvidia’s CEO had his thumb on the world of AI. An extramarital affair with a suspected Chinese spy may put all of that at risk.

Wired AI.title: Jensen Huang Hired a PR Firm Known for Handling Sex Scandals Last Year
Wired AI.description: The Nvidia CEO began working with consultants from Heller as early as October 2025, around the same time he was first linked to a suspected Chinese spy.

Wired AI.title: Authors Can Defend Against AI Allegations With ‘Paper Trail’ Tools. Is It Enough?
Wired AI.description: As the publishing industry wrestles with paranoia over the provenance of manuscripts, writers are caught in an impossible bind.

Wired AI.title: Bikers and Bug-Lovers Join Forces to Fight a New Google Data Center
Wired AI.description: As data center protests break out across Europe, a mismatched band of campaigners is trying to block Google from building a sprawling new facility east of London.

Wired AI.title: I Used NYT Cooking’s New AI-Powered Recipe Modifier, and It’s Actually Pretty Good
Wired AI.description: The New York Times has added a beta feature to its Cooking app that helps readers swap ingredients or adjust recipes to suit their needs. It mostly hits the mark.

MIT News — AI.title: MIT-led team receives funding to develop next-generation alternatives to modern weed killers
MIT News — AI.description: With up to $53 million from ARPA-H, the researchers will use AI to generate safer herbicides that reduce dependence on imports and improve the security of the U.S. food supply.

MIT News — AI.title: A single AI model simulates the behavior of many substances, from sliding sand to folding proteins
MIT News — AI.description: By learning how matter moves, the WorldParticle system could assist with developing soft robots, medicines, and more.

MIT News — AI.title: AI-assisted learning platform helps robots reason beyond literal commands
MIT News — AI.description: The new approach, known as FLEX, could lead to more intuitive, interactive household and assistive robots.

MIT News — AI.title: How to predict the behavior of molecules from scant data
MIT News — AI.description: A machine-learning approach called CheMeleon provides a practical way to develop new drugs or other molecules with much less detailed, expensive experimentation.

MIT News — AI.title: Clearing up a robot’s fuzzy memory
MIT News — AI.description: A new system identifies and corrects unreliable object descriptions stored in a robot’s memory, improving the robot’s ability to interact with its environment.

MIT News — AI.title: Building connections across the research infrastructure
MIT News — AI.description: MIT.nano and the Northeast Microelectronics Coalition gathered facility leaders and technology professionals from across the nation to explore ways to make shared-access facilities more connected.

MIT News — AI.title: Powering up for a pivotal moment
MIT News — AI.description: From a nuclear revival to qubits, the MIT Energy Initiative’s annual research conference tracked deployment of today’s technologies to discovery of tomorrow’s breakthroughs.

MIT News — AI.title: Regina Barzilay and Jim Collins win Pritzker Prize for AI and Science Research Excellence for work in AI-enabled antibiotic discovery
MIT News — AI.description: The MIT professors collaborated to identify the first AI-discovered antibiotic, a scientific breakthrough that is widely recognized as a milestone in AI-driven drug discovery.

MIT News — AI.title: MIT affiliates named 2026 Schmidt Sciences AI2050 Fellows
MIT News — AI.description: Five MIT faculty members and two additional alumni are honored with fellowships to advance research on beneficial AI.

MIT News — AI.title: Q&A: Hey AI, who should I vote for this year?
MIT News — AI.description: MIT professors Adam Berinsky and Chara Podimata discuss a new project to track how AI chatbots are responding to questions about the 2026 U.S. midterm elections.

MIT News — AI.title: 3 Questions: Why infrastructure is entering a defining era
MIT News — AI.description: Professor Ali Jadbabaie describes how AI, digital transformation, climate change, and complex geopolitics are forcing engineers and policymakers to rethink how infrastructure is designed, built, and managed.

MIT News — AI.title: Making machines that can listen
MIT News — AI.description: Professor Paris Smaragdis develops computers with superhuman hearing for applications like speech recognition, music understanding, and environmental monitoring.

MIT News — AI.title: Learner collaborates with MIT peers to develop book of AI insights
MIT News — AI.description: Prabha Jha used her experience with MIT Open Learning’s program for senior executives to develop AI solutions for her employer, Verizon, and to write a book.

MIT News — AI.title: At New York Climate Week 2026, MIT connects with a global network
MIT News — AI.description: A cross-section of the MIT community convened discussions on topics ranging from data centers and super pollutants to agriculture and education.

MIT News — AI.title: At MIT, Martha Minow speaks on sustaining democracy, both by using and overcoming AI
MIT News — AI.description: In Compton Lecture, the distinguished legal scholar warns of potential “loss of the Enlightenment” while suggesting ways innovations can meet our civic and cultural needs.
